Summary of what we're sending now: a completed questionnaire spreadsheet (redwood_iam_questionnaire_v1.xlsx) with item-level answers, a short implementation note on SCIM group-mapping, and our SSO metadata file for SAML (redwood_sso_metadata.xml). High-level callouts:

- SCIM: SCIM 2.0 Provisioning for users and groups is supported, with configurable group-to-role mapping and optional tenant-scoped prefixes.

- Audit/Retention: Token- and request-level logs retained for 13 months by default; can be extended to 36 months under enterprise/Private plans. Logs are exportable to customer SIEM via syslog or S3 export.

Elena — quick technical follow-up on a few items you flagged in the questionnaire: 

1) SCIM groups and multi-tenancy- Our SCIM implementation supports group assertions and group provisioning using standard SCIM Group resources. For multi-tenant customers we recommend either:
  a) tenant-prefixed group names (e.g., zenitya_sales, zenitya_engineering) — simplest when your IdP can emit name prefixes; or
  b) SCIM Group custom attribute (urn:redwood:tenant) to tag groups — useful if you can't change names.

  We can provide a sample mapping script (Python + simple transformation) and a one-page diagram. I attached an example mapping CSV internally; I'll put the diagram in the shared Drive.

2) Role provisioning and delegated admin- Roles in Redwood are defined as sets of capabilities (e.g., model-deploy, route-edit, billing-view). You can map IdP groups to Redwood roles via SCIM or just-in-time SAML/OIDC claims. Delegated admin is achieved through scoped admin roles + temporary elevation tokens (we track elevation via audit entries).

3) SAML metadata and automated ingestion- We expose SP metadata at the provided sitemap URL and accept IdP metadata uploads. For automation, we support metadata endpoints and a POST-based metadata exchange API.

If you'd like, we can run a 30-minute technical session (demo of SCIM provisioning against a sandbox tenant) — happy to schedule next week.

Hi Elena — answering the clarifications from our side so procurement/security have concrete responses: 

1) KMS / Bring Your Own Key
- Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations. We have templates and runbooks for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and Google Cloud KMS. For Dedicated (reserved capacity) we can also integrate with customer-managed keys via a secure key-escrow flow; for fully on-prem, keys remain in your HSM. We'll provide architecture notes in the implementation pack.

2) Audit logs and immutability
- We provide an append-only export capability to a customer-owned S3 bucket with object-lock (WORM) recommended. For hosted customers we retain audit logs for 13 months; for enterprise/private customers we can configure longer retention and S3 object-lock export for immutability guarantees.

3) SCIM group deletion
- Soft-delete is supported: group deletions can be configured to mark groups as inactive for a configurable quarantine window (default 30 days) before permanent deletion, and role bindings are suspended during quarantine.

Next steps: Vanessa — I'll prepare a short implementation note (1-2 pages) describing KMS options and the S3 export flow. I will also attach the sample SAML metadata we referenced. Elena — if procurement can share the specific MSA redlines, legal can start a review; we'll also include a DocuSign link for the standard SOW/NDA if helpful.
